  Night: may steal a token from another player (a visit). It happens at the end of the night, after that night's
  token use, so a token used tonight can't be stolen. The stolen token is gone (you can't use it). You are told
  whether you stole one, not its kind; they are told which kind they lost. If they have no tokens, nothing
  happens and they aren't told. A steal from a player who dies that night still takes the token and counts (R10).
  Win: iff you steal tokens from 3 different players (a second steal from the same player takes nothing). If you
  are alive then, the moderator reveals you at once and you leave the game (as for the Executioner). If you died
  that night, you still win and nothing is revealed.

Vulture
  Win: alone, if you are alive at the start of a Day (after the night's deaths) and your threshold or fewer players
  are alive, counting yourself. The game then ends at once and everyone else loses (wins already earned by roles
  that never block wins still count, R1). Your threshold starts at 2.
  Night: may visit another player. If they die that night (by any cause, end-of-night effects included), you are
  told at the end of the night that they died and their role (exact-role check, R19; nothing more if a Mortician
  cleaned them), and you get the first of these power-ups you don't have yet: +1 to your threshold, Standard
  Defense, +1 to your threshold, Strong Defense, then +1 to your threshold for each later one. Your threshold
  never goes above max(floor(N/3), 2), where N is the number of players at the start of the game; a power-up that
  would raise it further is skipped. If they don't die, nothing happens and you are told so.

Decoy
  Never blocks wins (R1).
  Win: iff you die at night. You lose if you die by Day or the game ends with you alive.
  If an attack killed you at night, the next Day's announcements say you were the Decoy and name 3 players: every
  player whose attack would have killed you on its own (3 of them at random if there were more), then random other
  players alive at the start of that Day to make 3 (fewer if not enough are left). The names are in random order,
  and the announcement doesn't say how many of them attacked you. Your cause of death and last will show as usual.

=== PART 7: TRAITS ===

R24 (Traits)
Some players also have a trait: an extra ability on top of their role. You are told your own trait at the start
(except a hidden trait, which says so); nobody else is told, not even your teammates, and whether a game has any
traits is secret. Investigations never see traits: they report roles and alignments only. A trait stays with you if
your role changes. Traits are always true: a Roleplayer's trait is real even though its role isn't. A player may
have more than one trait, but never the same one twice. Each trait below says who can get it (Who), whether it is
hidden from its holder (Hidden), whether at most one player in a game has it (Unique), what it does (Effect) and
which traits nobody holds together with it (Never with). A trait's night action is used in addition to your role's
own, and a role-block stops it too.

--- Village players only ---

Martyr
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the announcement of your death also says you were a Martyr and names every player whose
  vote counted as Guilty in your trial. Your role stays hidden. A Martyr who dies any other way shows nothing.

Cursed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you die, a random living Good player (if any) is dealt a Divine Attack at the end of the night: the
  night you died, or the night after the Day you died. It comes after all of that night's other actions and attacks,
  so the victim is drawn from the Good players still alive then, and it counts as a death that night. Its cause is
  "a curse". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Avenger
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you are killed at night, every player whose attack would have killed you is dealt a Basic Attack (an
  Astral Visit) that same night. Defense and protection apply as usual (R3); a kill's cause is "Avenger". Attacks
  that weren't fatal on their own, and deaths by Day, set nothing off. It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't
  stop it.

Kindred
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn up to two random other players whose votes counted the
  same way as the vote you cast (if fewer did, you learn that). It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Remorseful
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Guilty in a trial and that player is hanged and was Village (their true alignment), you die at
  once; the cause is "remorse". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks
  counts it.
  Never with: Zealot.

Ashamed
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: If you vote Innocent in a trial and that player is hanged and wasn't Village (their true alignment: Yakuza
  or Neutral), you die at once; the cause is "shame". It goes by the vote you cast. It isn't an attack, so nothing
  that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Merciful or Turncoat.

Faultline
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: After each trial vote you cast, you privately learn one random other player whose vote counted as Guilty
  and one whose vote counted as Innocent (if all the others voted one way, you learn that). It needs no action, so a
  role-block doesn't stop it.

Notorious
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19). Checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count,
  aren't fooled.
  Never with: Turncoat.

Stolen Blade
  Who: Village players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may attack another living player with a stolen Katana: a Standard Attack,
  besides your role's own action. It is an action and a visit by you, and it looks exactly like the Yakuza's Katana
  attack: a kill's cause is "Katana", and a surviving target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana.
  You learn only whether it killed. A role-block stops it, and then it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed.

Paranoid
  Who: Village players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/4, you are told you were attacked and survived, though nobody attacked
  you. The made-up attack is the Katana's 2/3 of the time, and otherwise a Vigilante's or a Serial Killer's (always
  the Katana's when neither role can be in the game); it is worded like a real one. Nothing else happens: it isn't a
  visit or an attack, and nobody else learns of it.
  Never with: Oblivious.

Turncoat
  Who: Village players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise, even if the Village wins.
  Alignment checks see you as Evil (R19); checks that see true alignment, such as the Census Taker's count, see you
  as Good. You stay Village in every other way: you aren't in the Yakuza's chat or Katana votes, you don't know who
  the Yakuza are, and they aren't told about you. The game's end ignores you, like a role that never blocks wins
  (R1): it ends when the other living players are all Village or all Yakuza.
  Never with: Ashamed, Notorious, Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Spiteful.

Spiteful
  Who: Village players only, except a Saint.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: If you are hanged, from then on you win only if the Yakuza win (alive or dead), and you lose otherwise,
  even if the Village wins. Until then you win with the Village as usual, and dying any other way changes nothing.
  Nobody is told you switched, and your will is revealed as usual.
  Never with: Rival, Selfish, Selfless or Turncoat.

--- Yakuza players only ---

Spare Blade
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may make one extra Katana attack on another living player, whoever holds the
  Katana and besides its own attack (which the Yakuza still choose as usual, R8). It is Standard, an action and a
  visit by you, and its target learns only that they were attacked with the Katana. A role-block stops it, and then
  it isn't used up.
  Never with: Armed or Berserker.

Usurper
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Unique: at most one player in a game has it.
  Effect: You win only if the Yakuza win while you are the only Yakuza alive, and then you take the win alone: the
  other Yakuza, alive or dead, don't win. If the Yakuza win with another Yakuza alive, they win and you don't. Your
  teammates aren't told.
  Never with: Selfish or Selfless.

Shaky
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Every Katana attack you make (the Katana's own while you hold it, or a Spare Blade attack) is level None,
  so it never kills (R3); it is still an attack and a visit.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Katana Master.

Katana Expert
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its own attack Strong instead of Standard.
  Choose it with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at
  the end of that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along
  with the attack, and it isn't used up.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Master or Shaky.

Katana Master
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Like Katana Expert, but the attack is Divine, which no Defense, protection, trap or charm stops.
  Never with: Berserker, Katana Expert or Shaky.

Berserker
  Who: Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, on a night you hold the Katana, you may make its attack rampage: besides its own attack, it
  makes a Standard Katana attack on every other player who visits its target that night, whatever their faction.
  These attacks on visitors aren't visits, and Astral Visits aren't visits, so their makers aren't attacked. Choose it
  with your night action and name the player the Katana attacks; it works only if you hold the Katana at the end of
  that night and it attacks that player, and only then is it used up. A role-block on you stops it along with the
  attack, and it isn't used up. Each attacked player learns only that they were attacked with the Katana; you learn
  how many players the rampage attacked and how many of those attacks killed, not who the visitors were.
  Never with: Katana Expert, Katana Master, Shaky or Spare Blade.

--- Village and Yakuza players only ---

Armed
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: Once per game, at night, you may fire a hidden gun at another living player: a Basic Attack. It is an
  action and a visit, and a role-blocked shot isn't used up. You learn only whether it killed its target. A kill's
  cause is "a hidden gun".
  Never with: Spare Blade or Stolen Blade.

Bonded
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random Village or Yakuza player are bonded, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role or faction). If either of you dies, the other dies of heartbreak at once (its cause is
  "heartbreak"). Heartbreak isn't an attack, so nothing that reacts to attacks counts it.
  Never with: Rival.

Rival
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You and one other random player of your own faction are rivals, and each of you is told the other's name
  (not their role). Each of you wins only if your faction wins and the other has died by the end; whether you are
  alive doesn't matter. Your faction's win doesn't change.
  Never with: Bonded, Spiteful or Turncoat.

Selfish
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are alive at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you
  just don't share it if you died.
  Never with: Selfless, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

Selfless
  Who: Village and Yakuza players only.
  Effect: You win only if your faction wins and you are dead at the end. Your faction's win doesn't change; you just
  don't share it if you're alive.
  Never with: Selfish, Spiteful, Turncoat or Usurper.

--- Any player ---

Grudge
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: If you are hanged, the next night one random player whose vote counted as Guilty in your trial, among
  those alive when that night begins, is dealt a Standard Attack (an Astral Visit). Defense and protection apply as
  usual. A kill's cause is "a grudge". It needs no action, so a role-block doesn't stop it.

Loud
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You earn 1.5 times the usual speaking budget each round, and your cap is 1.5 times the usual (R22). Your
  prices and trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Curt
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: The length part of your message prices (R22) is doubled, so long messages cost you much more; each
  message's base fee, nominations and your trial-only budget are the usual ones.

Confidant
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Once per game, on one of your own Day turns, you may send one private message hidden: nobody else is told
  it was sent, and the public ledger doesn't count it. Its recipient sees that it was hidden. Players who hear
  private messages (e.g. the Wiretap) still hear it, also marked hidden.

Zealot
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Every Guilty/Innocent trial vote you cast counts as Guilty, whatever you vote, including in your own
  trial. Your nomination (Yes/No) votes are unchanged. Your private reminder shows both the vote you cast and how it
  counted, and everything that reports how you voted (e.g. the Auditor, a Martyr's announcement) uses the vote as
  counted. A Fixer's reversal doesn't change it.
  Never with: Merciful or Remorseful.

Merciful
  Who: Any player whose role doesn't change how much their own trial vote counts.
  Effect: Like Zealot, but your trial votes always count as Innocent.
  Never with: Ashamed or Zealot.

Drowsy
  Who: Any player whose role has a night action and can be role-blocked.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: On each night, with probability 1/2, you are role-blocked (R9) with no blocker. On those nights you are
  told you were role-blocked, as with any role-block.

Stocked
  Who: Any player whose role starts with tokens and can ever have more than it starts with.
  Effect: You start with one more of each kind of token your role starts with.

Disguised
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: You are told a Village role (never your own), drawn at the start. Every exact-role check (R18) sees you as
  that role instead of yours, alive or dead; alignment checks still see your true alignment.

Narrow Escape
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: Once per game, on the first night an attack that isn't Divine would kill you (after Defense, protection,
  traps and charms), you survive: every non-Divine attack on you that night fails instead. It works like Strong
  Defense on every night until then, so a night when nothing would have killed you (e.g. a Medic stopped the attack)
  doesn't use it up. Divine Attacks and deaths by Day aren't stopped. You are told about the failed attacks as for
  any others (R3).

Oblivious
  Who: Any player.
  Hidden: you aren't told you have this trait.
  Effect: You are never told about an attack you survive.
  Never with: Paranoid.

Sleepwalker
  Who: Any player.
  Effect: Every night you visit one random other living player, besides any action of your own; code draws it, and
  you aren't told whom. It does nothing but visit: anything that sees or reacts to visits (R6), such as a Tracker, a
  Lookout or a Veteran's alert, counts it. It isn't optional, but a role-block stops it (R7).

---

For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Don't tell() the Bloodhound anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Bloodhound who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the track op, which spends the token; code tells them the result at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Bloodhound anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Also, every night while the game has a Bloodhound, use the attacks op once with the attacker of every Attack that happened tonight, fatal or not: the Katana holder for the Katana, a Vigilante's shot, the Serial Killer, a Veteran's alert or a Werewolf's rampage once for each player it hits, a Trapper's trap, an Arsonist's ignite, a Ritualist's attack (one entry per attack; repeats allowed; [] if there were none). Leave out role-blocked attackers, Jester revenge, a Cursed player's curse and an Avenger's attack (code counts those). Code counts them for the Bloodhound's result, which it also gives on nights with no token.
- A Coroner who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the examine op, which spends the token; code tells them the role and tokens left. Don't tell() the Coroner anything about it. The target must have died before the night began. It is an Astral Visit, not a visit (R6): nothing that reacts to visits sees it.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- An Insomniac who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the stay_awake op, which spends the token; code tells them the roles of up to 3 random players from your record_visits list. Don't tell() the Insomniac anything about it. Staying awake is not a visit: don't put it in record_visits.
- Kitsune: a Kitsune with no swallowed attack who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) laid a fox charm on its target. Resolve the charm FIRST, before any other protection (Medic, Trapper, ...): use the kitsune_charm op with every non-Divine Attack on the charmed player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert, an Enforcer's attack or a trap's hit-back), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced, e.g. 'Katana', 'Serial Killer')}, [] if none. Code picks the one the charm swallows and says which: treat it as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), then resolve the other attacks normally. Several charms on one player: one kitsune_charm op each, every one listing all the attacks; code has them act in random order, each swallowing a different attack. A Kitsune holding a swallowed attack can't charm; if it acted with a target (and wasn't role-blocked), use the kitsune_release op: code says the attack's level and cause, and you resolve it like any attack by the Kitsune on that target (a visit). If it kills, kill with exactly that cause, by the Kitsune, katana false; a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Kitsune. Code tells the Kitsune its results; don't tell() it about the charm or the release.
- A Magpie who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the steal op; code takes the token at the end of the night, after this night's token use, and tells both of them. Don't tell() the Magpie anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- Mirror Maker: a Mirror Maker who acted on another player (and wasn't role-blocked) placed a mirror on them (it spends a token). Resolve it right after any fox charm (Kitsune) and before traps and Defense: use the mirror op with every non-Divine Attack on the mirrored player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert or an Enforcer's attack), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}, [] if none. Don't list the attacks code reflects (below). Code says which attacks the mirror stops (all of them, except one a fox charm already swallowed): treat each as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), so traps and Medics on that player have nothing left to stop. For each stopped visit, code says it is reflected: resolve it as an Attack of the same level on its attacker (an Astral Visit, never reflected again: a mirror on the attacker just stops it), against their Defense, protection, traps and charms as usual. If it kills, kill with exactly the stopped attack's cause, by the Mirror Maker, katana false (a reflected Katana attack reads as a Katana death); a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Mirror Maker. Several mirrors on one player: one op each, every one listing all the attacks; they stop the attacks together. Code tells the Mirror Maker its result; don't tell() it.
- A Prosecutor who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the prosecute op, which spends the token; code runs the trial when the next day starts.
- Code tells the Scout their result every night from your record_visits list; don't tell() them anything about it.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.
- Narrow Escape (a hidden trait, R24): resolve every attack as usual (Defense, protection, traps, charms). If after that a holder named below would die tonight from any attack that isn't Divine, they don't die: every non-Divine attack on them tonight fails instead, and you use the narrow_escape op, which uses it up. Tell them and each attacker as for any failed attack; a protector whose protection didn't stop an attack learns nothing from the escape. A Divine attack still kills them: give that kill divine=true (code refuses a night kill of a holder otherwise). A night with no lethal attack doesn't use it. Never mention the trait.
- Disguised (a trait, R24): every exact-role check (R18: e.g. an Oracle's or Ritualist's guess, a Mortician's clean) sees these players as these Village roles, alive or dead: Mallory as Party Animal. Alignment checks still see their true alignment. Never reveal a true role behind a disguise.

Resolve all actions simultaneously per the rules, following the R20 checklist (R10; visits R6, role-blocks R9, attack vs defense R3, investigation results R19, e.g. the Katana holder and Fabricator frames). Use apply_changes for deaths and token/status changes, tell() for each private result, and end_phase when done. Deaths you apply are announced publicly at dawn automatically, including the kill's cause, so make the cause just the source as the rules allow it to be known (e.g. 'Katana', 'Vigilante', 'Serial Killer', 'Trapper'). For each kill also set `by` to the player whose action killed them (the trap's owner for a trap) and katana=true for the Katana attack; these are recorded for analysis, never shown. Don't tell() deaths to all. Code tells each player who dies tonight that they were attacked and died, with the kill's cause, at the end of the night; you tell every attacked player who survived, and a player who died about any other Attack on them tonight, failed ones included (R3, R20 step 5). Tell each role-blocked player that they were role-blocked, even one with no night action or who chose not to act (R9). A role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because its target can't be role-blocked (R9): when it did, tell it plainly ('Your role-block on X failed: they can't be role-blocked.'); when it didn't, its result line is just 'You visited X tonight.', with no word on immunity or on whether the block took (no double negatives such as 'didn't fail'). Write private results in the present, about tonight ('You were role-blocked tonight'), never 'last night': they are delivered at the end of this night. Every player who used an ability gets a private result line, even when nothing else happened (e.g. 'You went on alert. 1 alert token left.'), stating any tokens they have left, except where a role note below says otherwise (e.g. code tells them, so don't tell() them a second result). Code tells the Yakuza which actions each of them chose and the Katana's holder and target (R8), so don't tell() them that; role-blocked Yakuza's Katana votes still count. Only the attacker learns whether the Katana attack succeeded: tell them. Update token counts for any tokens spent. Before end_phase, call record_visits once with every visit that happened tonight (R6, R20 steps 1-2), as [visitor, target] pairs, a self-visit as [X, X] (an empty list if there were none). Easy to miss: the Katana holder visits the Katana target (R8) besides any visit from their own role's action; automatic visits (a Sleepwalker's); a Seer's chosen pair is a visit to both players. Leave out the actions of role-blocked players, Astral Visits and actions that target no player.

Also handle these roles' effects, using random_choice for anything random:
- A Bloodhound who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the track op, which spends the token; code tells them the result at the end of the night. Don't tell() the Bloodhound anything about it. It is a visit to the target only. Also, every night while the game has a Bloodhound, use the attacks op once with the attacker of every Attack that happened tonight, fatal or not: the Katana holder for the Katana, a Vigilante's shot, the Serial Killer, a Veteran's alert or a Werewolf's rampage once for each player it hits, a Trapper's trap, an Arsonist's ignite, a Ritualist's attack (one entry per attack; repeats allowed; [] if there were none). Leave out role-blocked attackers, Jester revenge, a Cursed player's curse and an Avenger's attack (code counts those). Code counts them for the Bloodhound's result, which it also gives on nights with no token.
- A Coroner who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the examine op, which spends the token; code tells them the role and tokens left. Don't tell() the Coroner anything about it. The target must have died before the night began. It is an Astral Visit, not a visit (R6): nothing that reacts to visits sees it.
- A Fixer who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the fix op, which spends the token; code counts the player's trial votes tomorrow as the opposite; nobody is told. It is a visit to the target only.
- An Insomniac who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the stay_awake op, which spends the token; code tells them the roles of up to 3 random players from your record_visits list. Don't tell() the Insomniac anything about it. Staying awake is not a visit: don't put it in record_visits.
- Kitsune: a Kitsune with no swallowed attack who acted (and wasn't role-blocked) laid a fox charm on its target. Resolve the charm FIRST, before any other protection (Medic, Trapper, ...): use the kitsune_charm op with every non-Divine Attack on the charmed player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert, an Enforcer's attack or a trap's hit-back), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced, e.g. 'Katana', 'Serial Killer')}, [] if none. Code picks the one the charm swallows and says which: treat it as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), then resolve the other attacks normally. Several charms on one player: one kitsune_charm op each, every one listing all the attacks; code has them act in random order, each swallowing a different attack. A Kitsune holding a swallowed attack can't charm; if it acted with a target (and wasn't role-blocked), use the kitsune_release op: code says the attack's level and cause, and you resolve it like any attack by the Kitsune on that target (a visit). If it kills, kill with exactly that cause, by the Kitsune, katana false; a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Kitsune. Code tells the Kitsune its results; don't tell() it about the charm or the release.
- A Magpie who acted (and wasn't role-blocked): use the steal op; code takes the token at the end of the night, after this night's token use, and tells both of them. Don't tell() the Magpie anything about it. It is a visit to the target only.
- Mirror Maker: a Mirror Maker who acted on another player (and wasn't role-blocked) placed a mirror on them (it spends a token). Resolve it right after any fox charm (Kitsune) and before traps and Defense: use the mirror op with every non-Divine Attack on the mirrored player tonight (work them all out first, including attacks other actions set off, such as a Veteran's alert or an Enforcer's attack), each as {by, attack (its level), cause (how its kill would be announced), visit (true if it was a visit by its attacker, false if Astral or not a visit, e.g. a Veteran's alert or a trap's hit-back)}, [] if none. Don't list the attacks code reflects (below). Code says which attacks the mirror stops (all of them, except one a fox charm already swallowed): treat each as stopped (its attacker and target are told as for any failed attack, R3; its visit still happened), so traps and Medics on that player have nothing left to stop. For each stopped visit, code says it is reflected: resolve it as an Attack of the same level on its attacker (an Astral Visit, never reflected again: a mirror on the attacker just stops it), against their Defense, protection, traps and charms as usual. If it kills, kill with exactly the stopped attack's cause, by the Mirror Maker, katana false (a reflected Katana attack reads as a Katana death); a survivor is told they were attacked by that cause's role (R3), never by a Mirror Maker. Several mirrors on one player: one op each, every one listing all the attacks; they stop the attacks together. Code tells the Mirror Maker its result; don't tell() it.
- A Prosecutor who spent a token (and wasn't role-blocked): use the prosecute op, which spends the token; code runs the trial when the next day starts.
- Code tells the Scout their result every night from your record_visits list; don't tell() them anything about it.
- A Vigilante whose shot kills is told the victim's role by code (pass by=<the Vigilante> on the kill op); tell them only whether the attack succeeded and how many tokens they have left.
- Narrow Escape (a hidden trait, R24): resolve every attack as usual (Defense, protection, traps, charms). If after that a holder named below would die tonight from any attack that isn't Divine, they don't die: every non-Divine attack on them tonight fails instead, and you use the narrow_escape op, which uses it up. Tell them and each attacker as for any failed attack; a protector whose protection didn't stop an attack learns nothing from the escape. A Divine attack still kills them: give that kill divine=true (code refuses a night kill of a holder otherwise). A night with no lethal attack doesn't use it. Never mention the trait.
- Disguised (a trait, R24): every exact-role check (R18: e.g. an Oracle's or Ritualist's guess, a Mortician's clean) sees these players as these Village roles, alive or dead: Mallory as Party Animal. Alignment checks still see their true alignment. Never reveal a true role behind a disguise.

reasoning:
Trying to figure out whether Carol or Heidi holds the role in question. Since the game hasn't ended, at least one Yakuza (or another blocking Neutral) must still be alive among the living players, since otherwise the remaining group would just be Village plus Olivia and the game would already be over.

If Carol is honest about her claimed visit to Dave, that splits things into Dave's group and Bob's group, but Heidi still needs to be linked somehow — either as the holder herself or through someone visiting her, and Dave could also simply be lying about the grouping. If Carol were the holder, her own unclaimed action toward Heidi (something quiet like a Fixer, Diviner, or Fabricator move that wouldn't alert Heidi) would still make the visit pattern work. But Heidi being the holder is the cleanest fit, since her direct visit to Bob explains everything without needing any extra connecting visit — though I need to check how her earlier mirror action on Bob would have affected where the Katana attack actually landed.

But it's odd for Yakuza to kill their own teammate, so maybe Erin wasn't Yakuza at all — perhaps Erin was Village, killed by a Katana while Bob survived a separate one, which only works with something like a Spare or Stolen Blade. I'm also weighing whether Bob himself could be lying about being Vigilante and is actually Yakuza, since his claimed kills were Ivan and Mallory — but if Bob were Yakuza, he'd likely have killed differently.

I'm also reconsidering Erin's claim that Judy was Evil, since Ivan backed a similar story and Ivan was Yakuza, so maybe Erin was actually Village and Judy got framed, which raises questions about why Erin died on night three.

Erin's N3 death lines up with a Katana attack — a Yakuza move on a Sheriff — and that overlaps with Bob surviving a Katana hit the same night, suggesting a Spare Blade or Heidi's mirror reflecting the attack back onto Erin if Erin herself was the attacker. I'm also rechecking the D4 vote totals to see if being Fixed explains my two Guilty votes matching exactly, tallying Mallory's trial numbers to confirm.

If Heidi is Yakuza instead, I'd need another explanation for who killed Erin with the Katana on N3, like a Stolen Blade villager or some Bob complication — that gets messy fast, whereas Heidi's mirror story accounts for everything cleanly, so I lean toward Heidi being genuine. Carol voted Guilty on Niaj alongside Erin and Ivan, which I should weigh next.

Looking at Niaj's trial math: 6-4 with five stated Guilty and five stated Innocent means one Innocent vote got flipped to count as Guilty, and Erin's claimed "check" on Dave N2 could explain a fix like that. Carol also defended Mallory on D4 (and Mallory defended her back), Carol's N3 claim of tracking Dave turned up nobody, and Ivan's will says he watched Carol N3 as a Mortician — so if Ivan tried to clean Carol and Mallory claims she blocked him, I'm wondering whether that points to Carol actually being Yakuza.

I'm also trying to pin down Carol's role more precisely as a Tracker claimant: her N2 claim was tracking Alice and visiting nobody, while Dave's N2 put Bob, Carol, and Ivan in separate groups. If Carol were Yakuza, that raises questions about Erin holding the Katana and targeting Alice. Then there's the conflict between Carol's N4 claim of tracking Dave and Dave's own claim of being alone in his group — if Dave is honest, Carol's claim would actually place Dave, Carol, and Olivia together as a separate group from Bob's, which could still be consistent depending on how the groupings shake out.

Now I'm working through whether Heidi fits into Bob's group — someone needs to have visited her and linked her there. Otherwise a role whose only output is an end-of-night result gives the town nothing when killed on N1. Alternatively, tell players with end-of-night results to write a conditional will. For the Scout's single-group case, use clearer wording such as 'Everyone was in one visit group tonight (e.g. Erin)'. Add a short example of how Katana attacks are counted to the Bloodhound text.

answers.confusing_rules:
1. The Fabricator's rule doesn't say whether a framed player is told anything. The Fixer's rule says "Nobody is told", but the frame text is silent. On Day 5 the whole Village case turned on "Heidi was visited on N4 and told nothing". I had to guess whether that visit could be a frame, a fix, a Diviner or a steal from a player with no tokens. A list of which visits notify their target would have helped.
2. Scout wording on Night 3: "The players were all in one visit group tonight, including Erin." Adding "including Erin", a player who died that night, reads like a hint. It's unclear whether it's just a note that players who died that night count.
3. The Mirror Maker can't take any action once its tokens are gone. That's clear, but it's easy to forget that "no action" leaves you as a group of 1 unless someone visits you. That point shaped how the Scout's group count was read against me.
answers.missing_information:
1. The hardest thing to track was each player's stated trial votes set against the announced totals, across several trials in one Day. The ledger repeats long claim strings, but it has no compact table of player × trial × stated vote. I worked out the 3–4 totals on Day 4 by hand.
2. Which earlier claims had been backed up by mechanics and which rested only on one player's word. Olivia's "confirming" tracks turned out to be fake, and nothing marked that in the claims history.
3. Which Fixer token was spent when. I could only infer it.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. With 0 tokens left, I wanted to make some visit so the visit groups couldn't be read against me. The role gives no tokenless action, which is fine by the rules but left me with no answer to that read.
2. I wanted to keep a compact vote table in the notepad, but the 425-word cap made that tight late in the game.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
Nothing looked broken. Every result I checked afterwards matched the revealed actions. Night 3: my mirror on Bob stopped Erin's Katana and the reflection killed Erin. Night 4: Dave really was alone, and the 2 groups were correct. Erin's fix on Frank explains both 3–4 totals on Day 4.
The only oddity was the "including Erin" phrasing in the Scout's Night 3 result.
answers.suggestions:
1. Add a per-trial table of stated votes to the public ledger, next to the announced totals.
2. In each role's text, say plainly whether the target is told about a frame, fix, clean, mark or charm. A single cross-reference list would also work.
3. Mark claims that have since been withdrawn or exposed as lies (for example Olivia's Tracker claim) in the claims history, so players don't keep leaning on "confirmations" from them.
4. Make Scout result wording the same every night.

answers.confusing_rules:
- Mortician: the role text never says outright that you can clean only once a night. My teammate Mallory miscounted her tokens because of it (she thought one clean a night would use up both).
- The Lookout cover was harder to fake than I expected. I claimed "Grace was visited by: Judy". Judy pointed out that a real Lookout on a Katana victim must also see the Katana holder's visit, so the fake could be checked from public facts alone. That's correct under the rules, but nothing in the role text makes you see it unless you work out the visit model yourself.
- The Fixer's timing ("the following Day") and the Kitsune's "hold and release later" mechanic both took careful rereading.
- When there are fewer than three groups, the Scout's wording ("all in one visit group tonight, including Erin") names one player. It isn't clear whether that name means anything or is just the drawn name.
answers.missing_information:
- I was never told that Frank's fox charm landed on me on Night 1. That's correct under the rules, but it meant I couldn't predict that Frank's later claim, "N1 charm on Ivan", would tie me into Dave's visit groups.
- Doing the visit-group logic for the Cartographer and Scout by hand across 9 to 12 claims was hard. A teammate's claimed visits, the real visits and the public claims all had to be kept apart in a 425-word notepad.
- I had no simple way to see each player's stated votes beside the announced totals for every trial.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
- I wanted to plan with my team in a shared, durable way, such as a joint claims sheet that all four Yakuza could see. Instead we re-sent the same plans in chat every night.
- Before I posted a fake result, I wanted to check whether it contradicted facts that are publicly derivable (like the Katana holder's visit). There's no tool for that.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
- Nothing looked broken.
- On Night 1, Alice's Insomniac result named "Fixer" even though Erin used no Fixer action that night. Her only visit was the Katana attack. That's correct, because the Katana visit counts as a visit by Erin and the result shows her true role, but it's a strong and maybe unintended leak of a Yakuza role from a plain Katana kill.
- On Night 4, Bob's attack notice and his kill result came in one combined message, while on other nights they were separate. The format isn't consistent.
answers.suggestions:
- Add "one clean per night" to the Mortician text. Also add a note to the Lookout and Tracker text that the Katana holder visits its target, so a result that leaves the holder out of a Katana victim's visitors is impossible.
- Make the Scout's one-group wording clearer, for example "Everyone was in one group (drawn name: Erin)".
- Add a per-trial table of stated votes against announced totals to the public ledger.
- Tell Yakuza players explicitly that an Insomniac or exact-role check sees the holder's real role through the Katana visit.

answers.confusing_rules:
- Lookout plus Katana plus Mortician on one target: it was hard to argue cleanly in real time how many visitors a real Lookout on Grace should see. The rules allow the holder and the cleaner to be the same player, the Lookout doesn't count its own visit, and Spare Blade exists. Together these made my mechanical rebuttal look weaker than it was. In fact Ivan was the cleaner and was excluding his own visit. A short worked example in R6 or the Lookout text would help: holder and cleaner on one target show as two visitors if they are different players and one if they are the same.
- Scout wording on a one-group night ("all in one visit group tonight, including Erin") is a little unclear. The rules say you learn one name per group and the number of groups, but "including X" reads as if X were special.
- The Coroner can't act on Night 1, because no bodies exist before it begins. That isn't confusing, but it means a Night 1 frame on a Coroner can never be answered with a result.
answers.missing_information:
- As a Coroner on Day 2 I had nothing to show: no result, no visit and no tokens spent. My claim couldn't be checked at all, while two coordinated false results (Erin's Sheriff check and Ivan's Lookout watch) landed on me together.
- It would have helped to know whether anyone else in the game had a role that could confirm a "no visit" claim. Trackers and Lookouts were claimed, but none of them had looked at me.
- After I died I couldn't easily tell whether my will had any later effect. Nobody ever examined me, since the only other Coroner-type role was me.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
- I wanted to nominate Ivan first, or to put him on trial alongside me. Niaj nominated me before my turn came round again, and once that trial started the Day was effectively decided.
- I wanted some way to prove my role publicly, like the Mayor's reveal or a self-check. A Coroner has no such option on Day 2.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: None that broke the rules, as far as I could see. The full log matches the mechanics: Erin died to the reflected Katana off Heidi's mirror, Bob's Vigilante kill read Mallory's Party Animal disguise, the Fixer on Dave produced the 6-4 total and the Fixer on Frank produced both 3-4 totals, and Frank's hidden Confidant PM left no entry in the ledger. One oddity: Ivan, a Mortician, spent a clean token on his own teammate Carol purely as cover for his visit. That's legal, but it showed up later as evidence ("why would the Yakuza clean their own?").
answers.suggestions:
- Give the Coroner, and other roles that can't act on Night 1, something minor to do on Night 1, or let them examine a Night 1 death on the night it happens, so a Day 2 claim isn't completely empty.
- Add a short example to R6 and to the Lookout text covering how many visitors a target with a Katana kill plus a clean shows.
- When a nomination happens, show the accused how many of their own speaking turns they lost. Alternatively, guarantee the accused one public message before the Yes/No vote, so a nomination isn't instant.
- For hand-picked setups, a tip would help: four Yakuza with two Morticians and a Fabricator can easily hang a Night-1-framed villager on Day 2.

answers.confusing_rules:
- Magpie steal timing combined with token use: "after that night's token use, so a token used tonight can't be stolen". My teammate read this as "spending a token tonight protects you", but a Mortician can only clean once a night, so I still had 1 token left that could be stolen. It took some working out. One sentence saying the steal only checks tokens left at the end of the night would help.
- The Fabricator's frame is a visit (R6 default). Its effect on visit-group roles (Scout, Cartographer) is easy to forget. Carol's free N4 frame on Heidi linked her into Bob's group, and that link is what exposed her. The rules are correct, but nothing near the Fabricator text points this out.
- For a long time it wasn't clear to me whether a Disguised Mortician's result on a Vigilante kill shows the disguise. R19 says it does, and it did ("Party Animal"). It would be easier if the Vigilante entry said this directly.
answers.missing_information:
- The Yakuza night summary gives each teammate's chosen action but not the result. Until the Day I didn't know that Ivan's N3 action was a clean on Carol and not a hold, as we had agreed. A teammate quietly changing plan only shows up in the summary text, and I had to read it closely to spot it.
- My current token count was only in that night's result line. I had to track it myself in my notepad. A standing "your tokens: X" line in every prompt would help.
- It was hard to keep track of which public claims created visit links for the Scout's groups. A per-night summary of claimed visits in the public ledger would help everyone.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
- Coordinate with my one remaining teammate during the Day. Any PM is public metadata, so in practice it was impossible. That's working as designed.
- Check the Katana vote tally or holder confirmation before the night resolves, to make sure every Yakuza actually submitted the agreed vote.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: None that broke the rules. Everything resolved as written. The reflected Katana killing Erin was announced as a Katana death. The Vigilante kill on me read "Party Animal" because of my disguise. The Kitsune swallow on N4 and the Katana passing to Carol after Erin's death also worked as written. One small oddity: Ivan's private chat said he would hold on N3, but his submitted action was a clean on Carol. That was his own choice, not a bug.
answers.suggestions:
- Put a line in every prompt with the player's own token counts and trait reminders.
- Add a public-ledger section with each night's claimed visits (A→B), to make group/visit reasoning less error-prone.
- Note next to the Fabricator, Mortician and other "cover" actions that they are visits and show up to Scout, Cartographer, Tracker and Fortune Teller. Teams keep making free visits that end up exposing them.
- After the Katana vote, show the Yakuza a short confirmation of the agreed holder and target and whether everyone voted for it.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) Prosecutor (R4/Prosecutor text): the rules say the moderator announces "that someone is being prosecuted". It's unclear whether the announcement names the prosecutor or only the person on trial. On trial, I offered "a prosecution will be announced on Day 4" as proof of my claim. I wasn't sure that would actually prove anything to the table, since it doesn't tie the prosecution to me. 2) Zealot in my own trial: the rules are clear, but it was hard to work out how the trait should change my defence. My own vote lowers the bar to hang me by one, and other players had to keep that in mind. 3) Kindred timing: it wasn't clear whether Kindred results arrive before or after the trial outcome is applied, or whether a hanged player can still act on them. In practice I got the result but couldn't use it.
answers.missing_information: On trial, I had no running tally of the stated votes. I had to rebuild "stated Guilty vs. stated Innocent" myself from chat. The ledger lists claims but not the stated vote for each trial in one place, and a compact per-trial table of stated votes would have helped a lot. Also, as the Prosecutor I had no way to show my role during the Day, so my claim was untestable in the very situation where it mattered.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: After my trial vote, Kindred privately told me that Frank and Olivia had counted Innocent. That, together with the 6-4 total, pointed to a fixed or lying stated Innocent. But I was executed right away and couldn't add it to my last will or post it, so the Kindred info from my own trial was wasted. I wanted one last chance to update my will between the vote result and the execution, or at least to have trait results that land after the vote but before death get appended to the will. I also wanted some daytime way to prove a Prosecutor claim, for example spending a token on the spot.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. Every total matched the hidden actions. My D3 hang came out 6-4 because my Zealot vote counted Guilty and Erin's N2 fix on Dave turned his Innocent into Guilty, which is exactly what the rules describe. Dave's N3 Scout result read "all in one visit group tonight, including Erin". That's correct, but the wording is slightly odd because it names a player who died that night.
answers.suggestions: 1) Let a player write or update their will at the moment they go on trial and again after the verdict, or automatically add any trait results they get during their own trial (Kindred, Faultline) to their will. 2) Add a per-trial table of stated votes to the public ledger, next to the announced totals. 3) Make the Prosecutor announcement say explicitly what it reveals (target only, or prosecutor too), so a "prosecution test" can be judged fairly. 4) Think about not dealing Zealot to a role that has no way to prove itself in daytime: Zealot plus Prosecutor made my own trial nearly impossible to survive (I needed 5 of the other 9 to vote Innocent, and a single fix was enough to hang me).

answers.confusing_rules: Magpie: "Random setups include a Magpie only if at least a third of the roles have tokens" doesn't apply to hand-picked setups, so it wasn't clear whether this game had enough tokens left for a Magpie to win. A related point: a steal happens after that night's token use. That means a player who spends their last token that night shows up as "no tokens". It took some thought to see that an empty steal clears nobody. Also, if I was the Village's deciding vote, it wasn't clear whether hanging the last Yakuza would end the game while a Magpie was still alive. It does, because the Magpie never blocks wins. I only understood that from R1, and the Magpie role text never says what happens to an unfinished Magpie when the game ends. I believe it simply loses, but the role text doesn't say so.
answers.missing_information: As Magpie, the key thing I needed to know was who still had tokens. That depends entirely on unverified claims about token counts. Partway through, I had to work out by hand that every living claimant except Bob said they had 0, and that my only possible third target was Heidi. Under the real roles, Heidi was already out of tokens, so after Night 4 my win was already impossible. Nothing told me that. It was also hard to keep track of each player's stated vote per trial alongside the totals. The ledger only records claims that players chose to post.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted a way to slow the game down once I saw that the last hang would end it before I could make my third steal. The only tool I had was my own Innocent vote, and with 6 players it wasn't enough. I also wanted to see my own past votes in the ledger. I had to rely on my notepad for that.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing looked broken. A few small things: Dave's Night 3 Scout result read "all in one visit group tonight, including Erin", and naming a single player there seems odd. Frank's hidden Confidant PM was delivered and marked hidden, as the rules say. A Magpie that can no longer win, because no living player has tokens, isn't told so and doesn't leave. The Bounty Hunter and Hitman are told when their win becomes impossible, so the Magpie works differently.
answers.suggestions: 1) Tell a Magpie when its win becomes mathematically impossible, the way the Bounty Hunter's and Hitman's roles do, or let it steal some other resource (for example, a one-shot trait use) so the role stays live in token-poor late games. 2) Add a per-player "stated vote" column to the public ledger for each trial, next to the totals. 3) Spell out in the Magpie text that the game can end with the Magpie short of its target, and that the Magpie then loses. 4) Have the ledger show your own private votes.

answers.confusing_rules:
1) The Kindred trait combined with Zealot. Niaj had both traits. On Day 3 he cast Innocent, but Zealot counted it as Guilty. Kindred says "players whose votes counted the same way as the vote you cast." I read that literally and reported Frank and Olivia, who counted Innocent. The other reading, "players whose votes counted the same way yours counted", would have given Guilty counters. The rules should state which reading is meant whenever a vote-changing trait or a Fixer is involved.
2) Yakuza night summaries for Yakuza who die that night. R8 says "each Yakuza learns" the summary, with no exception for players who die. I gave no summary to Erin and Ivan on N3 or to Mallory on N4, because they had died. It isn't clear whether dead Yakuza should still get it.
3) A Mortician cleaning a teammate. Ivan targeted Carol on N3 so his fake Lookout claim would match a real visit. The Mortician text doesn't forbid this, so I allowed it, but the rules never say so.
4) Scout when there is only one group. The rules say "fewer than three groups: one name per group and how many groups." On N3 everyone was linked, so I gave one name (Erin) in a one-group sentence. That works, but the wording for the one-group case isn't specified.
5) Insomniac and the Katana. On N1 the Insomniac result listed "Fixer" even though the Fixer took no action of her own. That was correct, because the Katana visit is Erin's visit and shows her true role. Players can read it as evidence that a fix happened, though, and Alice did just that. The Insomniac text could note that a role listed may have visited only through the Katana.
answers.missing_information: I had no built-in visit graph to check the Cartographer/Scout groups, so I built them by hand each night. The groups were: N1 {Carol,Judy}, {Erin,Grace,Ivan,Frank,Olivia} plus singletons; N2 one large group of 7 plus Bob, Ivan, Mallory and Niaj alone; N3 everyone in one group; N4 a group of 6 plus Dave alone. I also had no running token ledger. I had to work out by hand that on N3 Bob spent a token first and the Magpie then stole one, taking him from 3 to 2 to 1, and that Mallory went from 3 to 2 to 1. And I had no single view of standing modifiers: who was fixed on which Day (Dave on D3, Frank on D4), which framings were active, Heidi's tokens, and Frank's held swallowed attack. I needed all of these to check vote totals like 6-4 and 3-4, and I had to rebuild them from the log.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted an automatic check of each trial total against the true vote modifiers (Zealot, Fixer, Mayor, Ballot Stuffer) before announcing it. I also wanted a way to send several night results to one player as a single ordered message: Bob's N3 kill came as two separate messages.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1) Duplicate kill feedback. On N3 Bob got "Your Basic shot at Ivan killed them... leaving you 2" and then, separately, "Your shot killed Ivan. Their role was Mortician." On N4 the token line and the kill line were merged into one message, and a separate role message followed. The format was inconsistent and partly repeated.
2) Inconsistent tense. On N1 Erin got "Your Katana attack on Grace succeeds: they die." On N2 she got "succeeded."
3) The Mortician feedback format changed between nights: N3 said "Carol did not die tonight" and N4 said "Bob did not die tonight, so nothing was cleaned."
I re-checked every result I gave against the rules (the mirror reflection killing Erin, the Kitsune swallow on Bob, the Disguised Mallory reading Party Animal, all Scout groups, Bloodhound's count of 1 on N1, the Insomniac draws, every trial total, and the game-end check with the Magpie ignored). All were consistent with the rules. Olivia's Narrow Escape never triggered.
answers.suggestions:
- Give the moderator automatic helpers: a visit graph and group calculator, a token ledger that orders token use before Magpie steals, and a vote-count validator that applies Zealot, Merciful, Fixer, Ballot Stuffer and Mayor.
- Clarify in the rules what Kindred and Faultline mean by "cast" versus "counted" when a vote is changed.
- State whether Yakuza who die that night still get the night summary, and that Morticians (and other Yakuza roles) may target teammates.
- Standardise the result templates: one message per action, with a consistent tense and token-count line.
- Add a note to the Insomniac text that a listed role may have visited only through the Katana.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Steal on Nights 1-2, while almost everyone still has tokens. Pick players who say they haven't used their tokens (for example a Prosecutor who says 'tokens unused') or quiet players who have no reason to spend tonight. Never steal from a passive role such as a Scout, or from someone who just claimed they spent their last token. Each empty steal costs you a night, and these games often end by Night 4-5.

A steal resolves after that night's token use. A target who spends their last token on the night you visit comes back 'no tokens'. Aim for players who are hoarding tokens, not players who are about to spend them.

lessons.applies_to: Neutral roles that need the game to last (Magpie and others)
lessons.tip: Once the Yakuza are down to 1-2, every hang can end the game before you've won. Keep your Neutral identity hidden as long as you can, because confessing takes your vote out of the swing calculation. Push for 'test it tonight' delays early, before the town has enough mechanical evidence to ignore you.

A fake investigative claim survives longest when it only confirms claims other players have already made, such as a track that matches a protector's stated target. It can't break, but once you're exposed, every result it 'confirmed' loses its support. Expect that to be used against you.

Combine visit-group results (Scout or Cartographer) with protector notices. A survived attack plus 'swallowed' or 'stopped' feedback pins down which protector is real. The player left over in the attacker's group is the holder.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't shoot a confessed Neutral that never blocks wins.
tips_feedback.why: After I confessed to being the Magpie, Bob spent his last token on Mallory, not me, and the town left me alive. Confessing kept me safe, though it didn't get me my third steal.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens the first time they can change a vote or remove a threat.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi put her last mirror on Bob on N3, and it reflected the Katana onto Erin. Bob's shots took out Ivan and Mallory. Fast token use won it for the Village, and it also left very few tokens for me to steal.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: Don't defend a doomed teammate: vote Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and Mallory defended each other on D4. That linked them, and the town hanged Carol once the other links fell apart.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, or that you will act or spend a token.
tips_feedback.why: The Village publicly said 'Olivia steals from Carol'. The Yakuza planned around it: Mallory would have spent her token. Their own outcome didn't depend on it, but the public plan let the Yakuza hide token holders from my steal.

output.reason: Post-game reflection: I lost as Magpie because two steals hit players with no tokens. The game ended once the town hanged Carol, the last Yakuza.

reasoning:
I ended up losing as Magpie — Carol was hanged, the Yakuza died out, and the Village won. My steals were wasted: Night 2 I stole from Dave (Scout, no tokens), and Night 4 from Carol (Fabricator, 0 tokens). I should've targeted players more likely to hold unspent tokens rather than guessing blindly.

Given how fast the game moved, I needed to track who was hoarding tokens — Niaj had two unused Prosecutor tokens through N3, which would've been a perfect steal target, while quieter claimed roles tend to sit on tokens longer. I should steal early (N1-N2) from passive-seeming players before they burn through their stock, since a target who spends their last token right before I steal comes back empty-handed. I also think I voted poorly by not protecting the last Yakuza enough to keep the game alive, and being outed as Magpie cost me influence — my fake tracker claim worked by luck rather than consistency with others' confirmations.

Other lessons stand out too: don't shoot a confessed Neutral that doesn't block wins, since Bob ended up helping rather than hurting me; Yakuza shouldn't publicly defend a doomed teammate, as Carol and Mallory's mutual defense backfired; and one-shot tokens should be spent proactively, like Heidi's mirror use on Bob that killed Erin and aided the Village. Announcing targets publicly seems risky too — the Village calling out Olivia's steal on Carol and Bob's cover on Mallory still ended in Mallory's death, so the warning didn't fully play out as expected.

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.applies_to: everyone, especially Vigilante, Coroner and other exact-role checkers
lessons.tip: A Village role in an exact-role result (a Vigilante kill, Coroner, Oracle) doesn't prove the player was Village, because the Disguised trait shows a fake Village role. A 'Party Animal' who held both nights, blocked only a player who is now dead, and voted with the proven Yakuza is a disguised Yakuza until behaviour says otherwise. Weigh that result against their votes and visits. Don't publicly call it 'my mistake' and clear their partners.

Your first shot should go at the claimant whose result is mechanically impossible. For example, a Lookout who reports a single visitor on a Katana victim when the holder also had to visit. A Basic shot there is cheap and very likely to hit Yakuza. Once you have claimed Vigilante, expect the Katana every night. Write your next suspect into your will before each night.

lessons.applies_to: everyone using Scout or Cartographer group results
lessons.tip: The Katana holder also uses their own role's action, so one Yakuza can link two separate parts of the board. When a group result leaves one 'visited nobody' claim as the only link holding the case together, suspect that claim. A tracker reporting 'visited nobody' on a passive player, posted after the group result was public, is the classic fitted lie.

A Magpie steal comes after that night's token use. A suspect can spend their last token that same night, and the steal then comes back empty. So an empty steal clears nobody, and a suspect who invites a 'steal test' is offering a test they can beat. Only a successful steal proves anything.

Once a killing role (Vigilante) has claimed publicly, put protection on them, and spread it so the Yakuza can't predict a single protector. Here a mirror on N3 and a charm on N4 each stopped the Katana on the Vigilante. The mirror reflection also killed the holder.

Use a prosecution token on the first night you have a reasonable suspect (e.g. a claimant whose result has a contradiction). Unused tokens prove nothing, they let opponents call you 'untestable', and they die with you. A Prosecutor who has never prosecuted can't show the role is real before it's too late.
