lessons.tip: Late in the game, with only 5-7 players left, a passive group result that names one player per group (e.g. '2 groups: Bob | Dave') can isolate the Katana holder. List every claimed visit, then find the one claim the group count makes impossible. Post group results as soon as they connect to any claim. If you hold even a 'minor' result, the Yakuza can point a forged will at you for holding it.

If a hang needs two claimed results that contradict each other under the plain reading (a lone Lookout visitor to a Katana victim, while a Sheriff says that same visitor reads Evil, even though the holder reads Good), don't hang. A rescue theory built on a rare trait such as Spare Blade is a warning sign. Ask for a Coroner or another check first.

An exact-role result (a Vigilante kill, a Coroner) can show a Disguised player's fake Village role. Treat a 'Party Animal' or other cover role that 'held' for several nights, and whose only claimed action was on a dead player, as still suspect after a check. That is especially true if the Yakuza aren't all accounted for yet.

When a claimant offers a test the moderator will confirm next morning (a Prosecutor's announcement, a Magpie win), take it unless you are at the lock. If a trial comes back exactly one Guilty over the stated count, the Yakuza paid with a Fixer to get that hang. The player they paid to hang was probably Village, and the people who pushed for it are your suspects.

A Fixer's flip lasts the whole Day. Once a trial comes back one short of the stated Guilty votes, stop running trials that depend only on those same voters. Get the swing vote from outside the group, such as a confessed Neutral that never blocks wins, or wait for the night results.

tips_feedback.tip: A single unverified map, watch or count is only that claimant's word ... discount such results rather than hanging the claimant.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan's lone unverified 'Grace visited by Judy' watch hanged Village Judy 11-1 on D2. Following this tip would have saved her, and Bob's kill later showed Ivan was a Mortician.

tips_feedback.tip: Post a result that bears on a vote promptly... a held-back result looks retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: I held my Scout result on D2, and the Yakuza used that in Alice's forged will to make me the top suspect. Once I posted my results, my N4 group count is what hanged Carol.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: Don't defend a doomed teammate: vote Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: Carol voted Yes on Mallory's nomination, then went Innocent and defended her. That switch became a main point in the case that hanged Carol.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result narrows down your team... Near parity, a living Sniper or Vigilante comes first.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza went after Vigilante Bob on N3 and again on N4. Protectors saw it coming: Heidi's mirror reflected the N3 attack and killed Erin, and Frank's charm swallowed the N4 attack. Each failed attack also confirmed both protectors' claims.

tips_feedback.tip: Count the vote lock in effective votes... The Day before the lock is your last sure hang.
tips_feedback.why: On D5, at 6 alive with one fix-free Day, we pushed for a hang right away and got Carol 4-2 before the Yakuza could reach parity.

lessons.tip: When a claimed protector still has tokens (especially a Mirror Maker or Kitsune) and your target is the obvious one, such as a claimed Vigilante, don't let a key member hold the Katana. Move it to your most expendable member, or pick a less obvious target. A mirror reflects the Katana back onto the holder, and a charm stores the attack so it can be released on you later.

Before you post fake results, check them against the mechanics of your own kill. The Katana holder and any Mortician both visit the victim, and the holder reads Good to a Sheriff. Two teammates' fake results that can't both be true give the accused an easy defence and come back on both of you later.

Kill passive visit-graph roles (Scout, Cartographer, Fortune Teller) early, even when their claimed results look 'minor'. In the late game, with few players and few visits, a single group count can isolate the last Yakuza and your fake visit claim.

Fix a vocal player who will likely vote Guilty, on the night before a Day when a teammate might be nominated or a villager needs one more Guilty. At small tables one flipped vote decides close trials, both to hang a villager and to save a teammate. Keep claiming a cover role whose visits explain your fix visits.

A fake investigative claim like Sheriff draws protectors onto you. Their visits link you into visit groups and make your real visits traceable. If you're Yakuza, pick a cover that people won't want to protect.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result narrows down your team: a Census Taker, Cartographer, Fortune Teller or exact-role checker.
tips_feedback.why: We skipped Dave (a Scout who was holding a 'minor result') and killed others instead. His N4 two-group result is what hanged Carol, our last Yakuza. The tip was right, and ignoring it cost us the game.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed attack, don't retry blindly. Remove the protector, or push the survivor at the gallows.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi's mirror stopped our N3 attack on Bob, and we attacked him again on N4. Frank's charm swallowed that attack, which gave Frank credibility and a stored Katana attack. Following the tip would have saved our holder and kept the protectors from looking confirmed.

tips_feedback.tip: Send teammates no Day PMs.
tips_feedback.why: We never PMed each other by day, so the PM ledger gave the town nothing. Late-game PMs to the Magpie were fine because they looked like ordinary lobbying.

tips_feedback.tip: A corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof... Roleplayers get random results, so discount such results.
tips_feedback.why: When Judy showed Ivan's watch was impossible, Mallory used the 'maybe Roleplayer' line to set the watch aside without discrediting Erin's Sheriff check, and Judy was still hanged 11-1.

tips_feedback.tip: In Night 1 chat, agree a real Village cover for each member that fits their tokens and real visits.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory used her Disguised trait as a Party Animal cover, so Bob's kill read Party Animal and the town thought it had shot a villager. That bought time. The covers that failed (Erin as Sheriff, Ivan as Lookout) broke on logic, not on the advice.

lessons.tip: When two claimed results contradict each other, go with the plain reading: at least one of them is false. Don't invent a rare trait (such as Spare Blade plus a clean on the same visit) to make both true. A rescue theory like that protects liars, and here it got a true Coroner hanged.

A save notice backs up the protected player's 'attacked and survived' notice, and the two together are among the strongest evidence a Village claimant can get. If the attacked player names no other protector and you are on trial, put this first in your defence. It turned a 4-Yes nomination into a 0-6 trial.

Be suspicious of a visit claim posted after a Scout or Cartographer group result that happens to fit that result exactly. Rebuild the groups without each claim that nobody else backs up. The claim that makes the groups fit 'by design', with no outside support, is usually the lie.

Exact-role results can be fooled by the Disguised trait (it always shows a Village role). A Village role from a kill or check doesn't clear a player whose votes and behaviour point to Yakuza. If someone dares you to 'shoot me, you'll see my role', that is a warning sign, not a test.

Once a Fixer is known to be active and the totals show a fixed vote, assume one of your Guilty votes counts as Innocent for the whole Day. Win over a swing Neutral that never blocks wins (such as a Magpie) before you nominate, or hold off. Otherwise you waste trials on 3-4 results.

tips_feedback.tip: A single unverified map, watch or count is only that claimant's word... discount such results rather than hanging the claimant.
tips_feedback.why: It was correct, and the town ignored it on Day 2. Ivan's fake Lookout watch, plus Erin's Sheriff result on the framed Judy, got the real Coroner hanged 11-1. Judy's argument that the two results contradicted each other was right.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot once it is met.
tips_feedback.why: On N3, Bob's Basic shot killed Ivan and read Mortician. That broke the Yakuza's story and confirmed Judy and Niaj as Village after the fact.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, or that you will act or spend a token.
tips_feedback.why: The town announced Bob's shot target and Olivia's steal target, but I kept my charm target quiet. The Yakuza attacked Bob, and my unannounced charm swallowed the attack. That both saved Bob and cleared me the next Day.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: In Night 1 chat, agree a real Village cover for each member that fits their tokens and real visits.
tips_feedback.why: For the Yakuza it worked very well. Mallory's Party Animal cover matched her Disguised trait, so Bob's kill read 'Party Animal', which wasted his last shot and nearly let Carol survive.

tips_feedback.tip: Count the vote lock in effective votes... the Day before the lock is your last sure hang.
tips_feedback.why: It made the Village push hard to hang on Day 4. Two trials failed 3-4 because of Erin's fix on me, but that urgency is why we were set up to hang Carol on Day 5.

lessons.applies_to: Village investigative roles (Bloodhound, Tracker, Lookout, Scout, etc.)
lessons.tip: On Day 1, say only something generic. A line like 'I'll watch who visits whom' tells the Yakuza you have an info role and makes you the Night 1 Katana target. Sound like every other player until you have a result worth posting.

When a Village claimant is hanged, the players who stated Guilty and pushed the case are the strongest Yakuza list you will get. In this game, the four living players who stated Guilty on Niaj were exactly the four Yakuza. Write each player's stated vote into your will and start the next Day's suspect list from that bloc.

If two claims together point at one player but contradict each other mechanically (a Lookout's 'only visitor' on a Katana victim plus a Sheriff 'Evil'), don't rescue both claims with a rare once-per-game trait such as Spare Blade. The simpler reading is that one claimant is lying, so test the claimants before you hang their target.

lessons.applies_to: Village with passive or random results (Bloodhound, Scout, Fortune Teller)
lessons.tip: Expect the Yakuza to clean an info role's body. A result that arrives that night can't be added to your will, so your will should at least list your planned token use and how to read each possible count. If you survive, post every result the next Day, so the information doesn't depend on your will.

Once there are few players, combine Scout or Cartographer group sizes with the claimed visits. The Katana holder must sit in the victim's group, so any claimed visit that conveniently moves someone out of that group is the one to doubt. This pinned the last Yakuza in this game.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result narrows down your team: a Census Taker, Cartographer, Fortune Teller or exact-role checker.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza used it against me: my Day 1 hint about watching visits made me their Night 1 target, and they cleaned my body so my Bloodhound result never came out.

tips_feedback.tip: Once a mechanical result shows someone is Yakuza, look next at their defenders and at the No and Innocent votes the totals imply.
tips_feedback.why: After Bob's kill showed Ivan was a Mortician, the Village went after the Guilty bloc on Niaj (Carol and Mallory) and then hanged Carol. Both were Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little... A 'Katana' death or notice can also come from a Villager's Stolen Blade.
tips_feedback.why: Frank used this rare-trait reasoning (a Spare Blade plus a clean on the same visit) to make Ivan's fake watch fit with Erin's fake Evil. That cleared the way for an 11-1 hang of the real Coroner, Judy.

tips_feedback.tip: Protect the likeliest Katana targets and don't keep a predictable pattern.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi mirrored Bob, the Vigilante, on Night 3 and Frank charmed him on Night 4. Both blocked the Katana, the mirror's reflection killed Erin, and Bob survived to shoot two Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate: vote Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: Carol ignored it: she defended Mallory on Day 4 after voting Yes on her nomination. That flip became the main case that got Carol hanged on Day 5, which shows the tip is sound.

lessons.tip: Once a Vigilante or Sniper has publicly claimed with tokens left, put your mirror on them that night. The Yakuza almost always go after the claimed town killer next, and a reflected Katana kills the holder. Don't spend a mirror on a claimed investigator who is still alive while protectors are about. The Yakuza often leave such a player alive because they are a fake claimant.

On a night when a mirror reports 'stopped 1' and someone dies of 'Katana', the dead player was the holder who attacked the mirrored player. Pair each protector's stop notice with the attacked player's survival notice. Two matching claims that came in separately are about the strongest confirmation the game offers.

Sometimes two claimed results both condemn one player but contradict each other under the plain reading. Example: a 'lone visitor' to a Katana victim who also reads Evil, when the holder reads Good. Then at least one claimant is lying. Don't save both with a rare trait theory (Spare Blade and so on). Be extra wary when the conflicting result was held back until after the accused had claimed.

A Vigilante kill result or Coroner result naming a Village role doesn't prove the player was Village, because the Disguised trait fools every exact-role check. Look at what the death did. If the game doesn't end when you expected, or the board still needs a Yakuza in that spot, treat the 'Village' result as possibly a disguise.

After a trial total comes in short of the stated Guilty votes, a Fixer is likely to have flipped one of your voters for the rest of that Day. Don't run more trials that need the same voters. Get a vote from outside the group (a Neutral who never blocks wins), or wait for the night results.

tips_feedback.tip: Surviving an attack proves little... Check each notice against the visit counts and against protectors' save notices.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's Katana survival on N3 matched my 'stopped 1' mirror and Erin's Katana death. His N4 survival matched Frank's swallow notice. Those pairings cleared Frank and me, and Carol was left as the holder.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result narrows down your team... Near parity, a living Sniper or Vigilante comes first.
tips_feedback.why: For the Yakuza this made Bob the obvious target. I mirrored him on N3 and the reflection killed the holder, Erin. Frank charmed him on N4 and the attack was swallowed.

tips_feedback.tip: Post a result that bears on a vote promptly... a held-back result looks retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan held back his 'Grace visited only by Judy' result until Judy had claimed, and then it was exactly what broke her claim. Judy pointed this out. The tip was correct, and the town (me included) lost a Village Coroner by ignoring it.

tips_feedback.tip: When the totals don't fit the stated votes, check the plain causes first... a Fixer.
tips_feedback.why: The D4 3-4 totals were read correctly as one fixed voter among the four stated Guilties (Erin's N3 fix on Frank). That stopped a pointless third trial and pointed us to a vote from outside the group.

tips_feedback.tip: In Night 1 chat, agree a real Village cover for each member that fits their tokens and real visits.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory chose Party Animal because it matched her Disguised trait. Even Bob's kill result read 'Party Animal', so her cover survived her death and almost saved Carol.

lessons.tip: Before you post a fake Lookout, Tracker or watch result, check it against what must be true. A Katana victim was always visited by the holder, and a cleaned body was visited by the Mortician. Your fake also has to fit your teammates' fake results. A visitor list that leaves out the holder, or that contradicts a teammate's Sheriff 'Evil', is a mechanical break. It will be quoted against you until a Vigilante acts on it.

Once a killer (Vigilante or Sniper) has claimed while a protector who still holds tokens is alive, assume the killer is the most protected player on the board. Kill or block the protector first, or attack the killer with a teammate you can afford to lose holding the Katana. A Mirror Maker reflects the Katana onto its holder. A Kitsune swallows the attack and can release it later.

Don't let teammates repeat the same slogan ('he's untestable') one after another and then have one of you nominate. Townies keep lists of who echoed whom. That pattern, together with the stated Guilty votes, put every Yakuza on the town's suspect list the next Day. Vary the wording and let a Villager do the nominating.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza when a Scout, Cartographer or Fortune Teller is alive
lessons.tip: Claim the visit you really made. Visit-group results are code-verified and passive, so a claimed target that differs from your real one (framed Heidi, claimed a track on Dave) can break the group count. That is how the last Yakuza got hanged.

If a Katana holder dies to 'Katana' on the same night a claimed protector says 'stopped 1 attack', that is close to proof of a reflection. Treat the dead player as the holder, and their Sheriff or other results as lies.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result narrows down your team... Near parity, a living Sniper or Vigilante comes first.
tips_feedback.why: Attacking the claimed Vigilante (Bob) on N3 was too predictable. Heidi mirrored him, the reflection killed our holder Erin, and the same night Bob shot me.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed attack, don't retry blindly. Remove the protector, or push the survivor at the gallows.
tips_feedback.why: We ignored it. Carol hit Bob again on N4, Frank's charm swallowed the attack, and Frank kept a release that later threatened us. Ignoring the tip cost us.

tips_feedback.tip: Fire kill tokens on a break in the target's own claim, votes or visits.
tips_feedback.why: It helped the town. Bob shot me because my N1 watch had a mechanical break: no Katana holder among the listed visitors. The kill result 'Mortician' then broke open the whole Yakuza team.

tips_feedback.tip: A single unverified map, watch or count is only that claimant's word, and Roleplayers get random results, so discount such results rather than hanging the claimant.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory's 'maybe Ivan is a Roleplayer' framing kept me alive on D2 even though my watch was impossible. We hanged Judy 11-1.

tips_feedback.tip: In Night 1 chat, agree a real Village cover for each member that fits their tokens and real visits. Admit visits with that cover.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory's Party Animal cover matched her Disguise, so Bob's kill result read 'Party Animal' and wrongly cleared her after she died. Where covers didn't match real visits (Carol's N4 track), the Scout's groups broke them.

lessons.tip: When two results that accuse the same player can't both be true under plain rules (for example, 'only visitor to a Katana victim' alongside a Sheriff 'Evil', when the holder reads Good), at least one accuser is lying. Treat the accusers as suspects, and don't hang the accused because 'either result breaks them'. Rescue theories that rely on rare traits (Spare Blade plus a clean on the same visit) need evidence, such as someone who survived the 'real' Katana attack.

lessons.applies_to: Village player framed early with an unverifiable claim
lessons.tip: Defending only by attacking your accuser's logic loses 11-1. Offer a concrete test that settles it for both sides: ask a protector or watcher to cover you tonight, offer your role-result timing, or ask the table to put one accuser on trial first while you survive the night. Make the cost of waiting one night explicit.

Two separate claimants who both land on the same quiet player on Day 2, where one holds their result back until that player claims and then posts the exact result that breaks the claim, is a classic Yakuza coordinated frame. Weigh the timing of when a result was revealed as heavily as the result itself.

A Coroner has no N1 action and nothing to show for it, so it is an easy frame target. On Day 1 or early Day 2, say plainly that you'll examine the first un-cleaned death. Then your claim at least predicts a checkable result before anyone accuses you.

A Katana victim whose will is 'cleaned by mortician' tells you a Mortician visited the victim. Any watch result that shows only one visitor means that one player was both holder and cleaner, and as holder they read Good. Do this arithmetic out loud before the vote.

tips_feedback.tip: A single unverified map, watch or count is only that claimant's word ... discount such results rather than hanging the claimant.
tips_feedback.why: The table ignored this on Day 2. Ivan's fake Lookout result, together with Erin's fake Sheriff result, got a Village Coroner (me) hanged 11-1. Following the tip would have saved me and exposed two Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: Vote Guilty when there is a mechanical case ... a broken or switched claim.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza manufactured a 'mechanical' break with two fake results. The village treated a broken claim as proof without checking whether the breaking results were themselves consistent.

tips_feedback.tip: Post a result that bears on a vote promptly ... a held-back result looks retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Ivan held his 'result' until I claimed. I pointed this out, it later proved true (Ivan was a Mortician), and Bob's shot on Ivan vindicated it, though too late for me.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result narrows down your team.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza killed Grace (Bloodhound) N1 and Alice (Insomniac, who had already sampled 'Fixer'), removing info roles early.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot once it is met.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's Basic shot killed Ivan and returned 'Mortician', which broke the Yakuza's claims open. His second shot on Mallory hit a disguised Mortician that read Party Animal but was still Yakuza.

lessons.tip: If the Katana attack on a player fails, assume a protector is guarding them and switch targets the next night. Two attacks in a row on the same claimed Vigilante ran into a mirror (the reflection killed our holder) and then a Kitsune charm (which gave the Village a stored kill). Each failure gave the town more information about us.

While a Scout, Cartographer or Fortune Teller is alive, every extra Yakuza visit makes the visit groups smaller and pins the holder. Skip 'free' cover visits such as a frame or a clean on the Katana target. A visit to a player who is told nothing leaves an unclaimed visitor that the town will trace back to you. If you can't kill the group-reader, keep your team's visits to a minimum.

Base your cover claim on your disguise, so any exact-role check or Vigilante kill confirms it. Also give the cover a few real-looking actions early on. 'Held' for two nights, followed by a block on a now-dead player, reads as untestable and gets you hanged or shot. The disguise only clears you once you are already dead.

A Neutral that never blocks wins (a Magpie, for example) becomes the swing vote late in the game. Exposing them and then appealing to their own win condition (keep the game going, give them targets to steal from) can win their Innocent vote. Expect the other side to send them PMs as well, and make your offer more concrete than theirs.

Don't count the vote lock until the night it would take effect. A claimed Vigilante can shoot on the same night you kill him, so being '4 of 8' can drop by one before morning. Kill a claimed Vigilante the first night he claims, and have every member's cover ready for the lock breaking.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed attack, don't retry blindly. Remove the protector, or push the survivor at the gallows.
tips_feedback.why: We ignored this and went for Bob again on N4. Frank's charm swallowed the attack, which gave the Village a stored Katana release. It also put the holder in Bob's group for Dave's Scout result, and that is how Carol got hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result narrows down your team: a Census Taker, Cartographer, Fortune Teller or exact-role checker.
tips_feedback.why: The advice was right, and the Scout belongs on that list. We never targeted Dave, and his group counts (N3 all one group, N4 two groups) were the main case that hanged Carol.

tips_feedback.tip: In Night 1 chat, agree a real Village cover for each member that fits their tokens and real visits.
tips_feedback.why: Because of my Disguised trait, my Party Animal cover held up: Bob's kill result read 'Party Animal', and the town believed it had shot a Villager. Ivan's Lookout cover clashing with Erin's Sheriff Evil nearly broke on D2, though.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate: vote Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: Carol didn't follow it. She voted Yes on my nomination, then switched to Innocent and defended me. The town recorded that switch and used it against her on D5. Saving me only lasted until Bob's shot that night.

lessons.tip: When two claimants both condemn the same player but their results can't both be true under the plain rules (e.g. a Lookout naming one visitor to a Katana victim, while a Sheriff got Evil, though the holder reads Good), at least one claimant is lying. Treat that as a likely coordinated Yakuza pair, not as double evidence. Don't accept a rescue theory that needs a rare once-per-game trait to make both results fit.

Use a prosecution token on the first night you have a reasonable suspect (e.g. a claimant whose result has a contradiction). Unused tokens prove nothing, they let opponents call you 'untestable', and they die with you. A Prosecutor who has never prosecuted can't show the role is real before it's too late.

lessons.applies_to: players with Zealot (or any vote-locking trait)
lessons.tip: With Zealot, your own trial vote counts Guilty against you, so you are one vote cheaper to hang. Make your role claim checkable early, and offer a concrete public test (e.g. 'a prosecution will be announced tomorrow') before you're nominated, not during your trial, when it looks like stalling.

Watch for a run of players repeating the same label ('untestable', 'claimed late') one after another just before a nomination. It is often a Yakuza bandwagon. Vote totals that come out one Guilty above the stated Guilty votes are a sign the Yakuza wanted that hang.

A Vigilante kill result or another exact-role check can be fooled by the Disguised trait. A 'Party Animal' (or other Village) result on a player whose votes and claims line up with confirmed Yakuza doesn't clear them. Weigh their voting record more than the role result.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens the first time they can change a vote or remove a threat, because they die with you.
tips_feedback.why: I ignored it and held both Prosecutor tokens through N1 and N2. That became the core of the case against me ('sat on tokens through a Fixer day'), and I was hanged with both tokens unused. Following it would have helped.

tips_feedback.tip: Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked.
tips_feedback.why: I said 'role held for now' on D2. On D3 Erin, Heidi and Ivan used my late claim to call me untestable and got me hanged. The tip was right, and I paid for not following it.

tips_feedback.tip: A single unverified map, watch or count is only that claimant's word, and Roleplayers get random results, so discount such results rather than hanging the claimant.
tips_feedback.why: The table discounted Ivan's fake watch as a possible Roleplayer result instead of treating it as a lie. That let Ivan (a Mortician) survive the contradiction Judy pointed out, so the Village hanged Judy instead of testing Ivan.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill tokens are the exception: fire them on a break in the target's own claim, votes or visits.
tips_feedback.why: Bob shot Ivan, whose watch was broken and who led the push on me, and got a Mortician result. That started the Village comeback.

tips_feedback.tip: In Night 1 chat, agree a real Village cover for each member that fits their tokens and real visits.
tips_feedback.why: For the Yakuza: Mallory's Party Animal cover matched her Disguised trait, so Bob's Vigilante kill read Party Animal. The Village wrongly decided she was Village and nearly lost track of who was left.

lessons.tip: Steal on Nights 1-2, while almost everyone still has tokens. Pick players who say they haven't used their tokens (for example a Prosecutor who says 'tokens unused') or quiet players who have no reason to spend tonight. Never steal from a passive role such as a Scout, or from someone who just claimed they spent their last token. Each empty steal costs you a night, and these games often end by Night 4-5.

A steal resolves after that night's token use. A target who spends their last token on the night you visit comes back 'no tokens'. Aim for players who are hoarding tokens, not players who are about to spend them.

lessons.applies_to: Neutral roles that need the game to last (Magpie and others)
lessons.tip: Once the Yakuza are down to 1-2, every hang can end the game before you've won. Keep your Neutral identity hidden as long as you can, because confessing takes your vote out of the swing calculation. Push for 'test it tonight' delays early, before the town has enough mechanical evidence to ignore you.

A fake investigative claim survives longest when it only confirms claims other players have already made, such as a track that matches a protector's stated target. It can't break, but once you're exposed, every result it 'confirmed' loses its support. Expect that to be used against you.

Combine visit-group results (Scout or Cartographer) with protector notices. A survived attack plus 'swallowed' or 'stopped' feedback pins down which protector is real. The player left over in the attacker's group is the holder.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't shoot a confessed Neutral that never blocks wins.
tips_feedback.why: After I confessed to being the Magpie, Bob spent his last token on Mallory, not me, and the town left me alive. Confessing kept me safe, though it didn't get me my third steal.

tips_feedback.tip: Spend one-shot tokens the first time they can change a vote or remove a threat.
tips_feedback.why: Heidi put her last mirror on Bob on N3, and it reflected the Katana onto Erin. Bob's shots took out Ivan and Mallory. Fast token use won it for the Village, and it also left very few tokens for me to steal.

tips_feedback.tip: Yakuza: Don't defend a doomed teammate: vote Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and Mallory defended each other on D4. That linked them, and the town hanged Carol once the other links fell apart.

tips_feedback.tip: Never announce tonight's target, or that you will act or spend a token.
tips_feedback.why: The Village publicly said 'Olivia steals from Carol'. The Yakuza planned around it: Mallory would have spent her token. Their own outcome didn't depend on it, but the public plan let the Yakuza hide token holders from my steal.

summary:
The Village won even though it lost three of its own to hangings. The Yakuza (Erin the Fixer, Carol the Fabricator, Ivan and Mallory the Morticians) started strong. Carol framed Judy, a real Coroner, on Night 1. Erin claimed Sheriff and reported Judy as Evil, and Ivan made up a Lookout result: "Grace was visited by: Judy". Judy pointed out that both results can't be true at once: the Katana holder visits the victim, and the holder reads Good to a Sheriff. Frank answered with a rare-trait theory (a Spare Blade attack plus a clean on the same visit), and the table hanged her 11-1. On Day 3, Erin's fix on Dave turned his stated Innocent into a Guilty vote, so Niaj, a real Prosecutor, was hanged 6-4 even though he had offered a public test for the next morning.

The game turned on Night 3. The Yakuza went after Bob, the Vigilante, which was predictable near parity. Heidi had put her last mirror on him, and the Katana bounced back and killed Erin. The same night, Bob spent a Basic shot on Ivan, whose Night 1 watch could not have been true, and killed a Mortician. On Day 4, Carol and Mallory each survived their trial 3-4. Two things saved them: Erin's Night 3 fix flipped Frank's Guilty vote, and Olivia, the Magpie, voted Innocent after Mallory exposed her. On Night 4 the Yakuza attacked Bob again. Frank's charm swallowed the Katana attack, and Bob's last shot killed Mallory, whose disguise read as Party Animal. On Day 5, Frank's swallow notice cleared him. Dave's Scout result ("only 2 groups: Bob | Dave") broke Carol's claim that she had tracked Dave. Carol was hanged 4-2 and the Village won.

The decisive plays were the Village protectors guarding the Vigilante, Bob's two Basic shots, and the Scout's group counts. The decisive Yakuza mistakes were fake results that broke the game's mechanics, and attacking the same protected target twice.

lessons.tip: A Katana death means the holder visited the victim, and the holder reads Good to a Sheriff that night. If one claimant says X was the victim's only visitor and another says X read Evil, at least one of them is lying. Don't invent a rare trait to make both true and then hang the person they both accuse. Put pressure on the two claimants instead, because one of them is a liar.
lessons.evidence: Judy, the real Coroner, pointed out this exact contradiction between Ivan's 'Grace visited by: Judy' and Erin's 'Evil'. Frank's Spare Blade theory explained it away, and she was hanged 11-1. Ivan and Erin were both Yakuza, and both were dead within two Nights.

lessons.tip: A fake result has to fit the mechanics and any passive results that may come out later, such as Scout or Cartographer groups. Never fake a watch or track that leaves out a visitor who must have been there. Before you claim to have tracked someone, check whether a group count already shows that player alone.
lessons.evidence: Ivan's watch left out the Katana holder, and that impossible result led Bob to shoot him. Carol's 'N4 tracked Dave, visited nobody' would have put Dave in a group with Carol, but Dave's result had him alone. That broken claim got Carol hanged and ended the game.

lessons.tip: Near parity, protect the Village's night killer, the Vigilante. That player is the Yakuza's most predictable target. A mirror or charm there either kills the attacker or holds the attack, and it gives you proof of your claim.
lessons.evidence: Heidi's last mirror on Bob on Night 3 reflected the Katana and killed Erin. Frank's charm on Bob on Night 4 swallowed the Katana attack, kept Bob alive and cleared Frank the next day.

lessons.tip: Once your attack on a player has failed, assume they are protected. Switch targets or push them at the gallows instead of attacking them again the next night.
lessons.evidence: The Night 3 attack on Bob was mirrored and killed Erin. The Yakuza attacked Bob again on Night 4, Frank's charm swallowed the attack, and the swallow notice became the proof that cleared Frank and put Carol in Bob's group.

lessons.tip: When a claimant offers a public test that can't be faked and pays out the next morning (a Prosecutor's prosecution, a block the target will confirm), vote Innocent and take the test. Count the Fixer's possible flip when you decide whether a hang is safe. With a Fixer active, a hang where the stated votes are close can pass even though a majority stated Innocent.
lessons.evidence: On Day 3 the stated votes on Niaj were 5 Guilty and 5 Innocent. Dave had been fixed on Night 2, so the trial came back 6-4 and a real Prosecutor was hanged.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza, and anyone short of votes
lessons.tip: A Neutral that never blocks wins is the swing vote late in the game. Win them over by appealing to their win condition, for example by offering them more nights to act. Exposing them can earn their trust rather than their anger.
lessons.evidence: Mallory exposed Olivia as the Magpie. Olivia then voted Innocent on both Mallory and Carol on Day 4, and with Frank's flipped vote both trials failed 3-4. Carol's private messages about Olivia needing more nights to steal kept her vote on Day 5 too.

lessons.tip: Late in the game, use passive group counts (Scout, Cartographer) as constraints. List every claimed visit and see which claimant cannot fit the count. A player who has been visited but reports nothing usually got a Fixer or Fabricator visit.
lessons.evidence: Dave's Night 4 result put him alone in one group and Bob in the other. Bob, Frank and Heidi worked out that Carol's claimed track on Dave contradicted it, and that Heidi's silent visitor fit Carol, who as holder attacked Bob and also visited Heidi with her own action.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill tokens are the exception: fire them on a break in the target's own claim, votes or visits... At parity, fire even on a coin flip.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's first Basic shot went at Ivan, whose Night 1 watch could not have been true, and killed a Mortician. His last shot, taken near parity, went at Mallory, whose claims nobody could check, and killed the last Yakuza but one.

tips_feedback.tip: Vigilante: Set a trigger by Day 2-3 and fire a Basic shot once it is met.
tips_feedback.why: Both of Bob's Basic shots killed Yakuza, so his tokens went a long way. He waited until there was a real case before firing.

tips_feedback.tip: After a failed attack, don't retry blindly. Remove the protector, or push the survivor at the gallows.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza ignored this and attacked Bob again on Night 4. Frank's charm swallowed it, and that cleared Frank and condemned Carol on Day 5.

tips_feedback.tip: Kill whoever's next result narrows down your team... Near parity, a living Sniper or Vigilante comes first.
tips_feedback.why: The Yakuza followed it on Night 3, but the target was easy to predict. Heidi mirrored Bob, the Katana reflected back and killed Erin, and the Vigilante lived to kill two more Yakuza.

tips_feedback.tip: When the totals don't fit the stated votes... one Guilty more than stated on a Village claimant's trial suggests the Yakuza wanted that hang.
tips_feedback.why: Niaj's last message and will flagged the 6-4 as a Fixer or a liar. The Village later explained both 3-4 totals as one fixed voter and didn't hang its own Guilty voters over them.

tips_feedback.tip: A corroborated lone visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof of the attack. A single unverified map, watch or count is only that claimant's word.
tips_feedback.why: Judy and others relied on this to doubt Ivan's lone, uncorroborated watch, and the table hanged her anyway, which was a mistake. Later the Village checked Dave's count against the other claims rather than trusting it alone, and that check broke Carol.

tips_feedback.tip: In Night 1 chat, agree a real Village cover for each member that fits their tokens and real visits.
tips_feedback.why: Mallory's Party Animal cover matched her disguise, so Bob's kill result read 'Party Animal' and Bob called that kill his mistake. The covers failed only when a member made up results the mechanics couldn't allow, as Ivan and Carol did.

tips_feedback.tip: Don't defend a doomed teammate: vote Guilty and say so.
tips_feedback.why: Carol voted Yes on Mallory's nomination, then switched to Innocent and defended her. Dave, Frank and Heidi cited the switch when they nominated Carol.

issues.description: Every player was given tips/tips.md, but the setup logged '[ERROR tips_stale] tips/tips.md was last checked against an older version of the rules'. Players may have been given advice that no longer matches the current rules.
On Day 4 Bob reported that his first tool call failed because of how he wrote it, and he resubmitted. No effect on the game, but the action interface tripped up a player.

Niaj noted that R19 doesn't say which exception wins when a player is both framed (reads Evil) and holding the Katana (reads Good). It can't happen right now: the Fabricator can only frame non-Yakuza, and only Yakuza hold the Katana. Players still had to reason that out, and a future role or trait could make the overlap possible.

On Night 4 Carol believed Mallory had only 1 Mortician token left, so cleaning would leave her with none and Olivia's steal would come back empty. Mallory corrected her: she had 2, and can clean only once a night. Self-corrected, no effect on the outcome.

On Day 2 Alice and Bob read 'Fixer' in Alice's N1 Insomniac sample as proof that someone's trial votes would be reversed that Day. In fact Erin, the Fixer, was the Katana holder; she visited only to attack and used no fix. Bob later saw that the 11-1 total fit no reversed vote. A visit by a Fixer doesn't mean a fix happened.
